result.topic_en: Euler sets up a simplified model of a column made of two rigid halves AC and CB joined at the middle C by an elastic hinge, loaded by its own weight and a horizontal force at C, and begins to determine the forces, the elastic moment and the angle of deflection.

items.quote: atque tam ex pondere columnae quam vi applicata C $c$, ad momentum flexurae relata, quaeri debet status iste inflexus, siue anguli deflexionis a situ verticali C A O et C B O
items.english: and from both the weight of the column and the applied force Cc, referred to the moment of flexure, this inflected state must be sought, i.e. the angles of deflection CAO and CBO from the vertical position.

items.quote: qui quidem inter se erunt aequales, quia partes A C et B C aequales supponuntur
items.english: which indeed will be equal to each other, since the parts AC and BC are supposed equal.

items.quote: erit angulus $ECe = 2\,\theta$, cui proportionalis statui potest vis elastri, siquidem hunc angulum tanquam minimum spectemus
items.english: the angle ECe will be 2θ, to which the force of the spring may be taken proportional, provided we regard this angle as very small.
